provisions.title: H.J. Res. 109
provisions.heading: Sole operative clause: congressional disapproval of D.C. Act 26–86
provisions.quote: That the Congress disapproves of the action of the District of Columbia Council described as follows: The Open Meetings Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2025 (D.C. Act 26–86), enacted by the Council of the District of Columbia on June 26, 2025, and transmitted to Congress pursuant to section 602(c)(1) of the District of Columbia Home Rule Act on July 7, 2025.
provisions.context:
H.J. Res. 109 is an introduced House joint resolution with one unnumbered operative clause. Ms. Hageman submitted the analyzed version on July 23, 2025, and it was referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. The clause identifies D.C. Act 26–86, records that the D.C. Council enacted it on June 26, 2025 and transmitted it to Congress on July 7, 2025 under section 602(c)(1) of the District of Columbia Home Rule Act, and states that Congress disapproves of the Council action. Introduction and referral did not themselves enact the joint resolution, so its formal disapproval remains contingent on the federal enactment process.

Source limits / honesty note: The supplied source does not reproduce D.C. Act 26–86 or the cited Home Rule Act provision, explain what the temporary Act changes, state the precise downstream legal consequence of disapproval, or supply a replacement rule, implementation step, reporting duty, quantitative target, or empirical outcome. It therefore supports only the literal goal and enactment-contingent effect below. It does not support claims about transparency, public access, meeting practices, compliance, costs, or agency workload. The formal legal act is categorical and one-time rather than a recurring empirical series, so this provision honestly has no forecastable metrics, series hints, stance matrices, or conditionals.
goals: Disapprove the D.C. Council's action approving the Open Meetings Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2025 (D.C. Act 26–86).

effects.text: If enacted, the joint resolution would express Congress's formal disapproval of the identified D.C. Council action. The clause does not say that D.C. Act 26–86 shall have no force or effect, repeal or amend that Act, prescribe replacement open-meetings rules, or direct an implementing actor.
